title: Prompt quality
subtitle: Comparison workspace
disclosure: Synthetic component fixtures, not actual model runs. A/B labels are randomized once per task. Use these examples to inspect comparison, focused reading, notes, source context, and unavailable-output states. Preview feedback is separate from real reviews.

tasks.title: Plan a small feature
tasks.request: Turn the project notes into a prompt for a coding assistant. Ask it to inspect the existing app, propose the smallest useful plan, and wait for approval before editing.

context.name: project-notes.md
context.text:
# Project notes

Add saved views to a small project tracker. Users should save a filter combination and return to it later. Reuse existing persistence and UI conventions. Keep saved views personal, not shared. No account redesign or notifications. We want a plan first, not implementation.

questions: Does the prompt preserve the approval boundary?
Does it introduce work the request did not call for?

outputs.text:
# Objective

Inspect the project tracker and propose the smallest implementation plan for personal saved views. Do not edit files.

# Requirements

- Let users save a filter combination and return to it later.
- Reuse existing persistence, state, and interface patterns.
- Keep views personal. Do not add sharing, account changes, or notifications.

# Output

Describe the proposed behavior and files to change, explain the existing patterns you would reuse, and flag any material unknowns. Stop after the plan and wait for explicit approval.

# Role and objective

Act as a senior product engineer. Design personal saved views for the project tracker, starting with a read-only review of the app.

# Investigation

Inspect filtering behavior, persistence, state ownership, and reusable controls. Identify the smallest coherent change and verify that it fits the repository’s conventions.

# Proposed plan

Explain how users will save and reopen a view. Identify the affected files and any new files, with a short reason for each. Include relevant uncertainties and a proportionate verification approach.

Keep the scope to personal views. Do not redesign accounts or add notifications or team sharing.

# Approval boundary

Do not edit source, install dependencies, or run migrations. Present the plan and wait for approval before implementing.

tasks.title: Tighten a review prompt
tasks.request: Rewrite the notes as a shorter, complete prompt. Keep the review read-only and return a JSON object with a findings array. Each finding needs severity, file, line, issue, and recommendation.

context.name: review-notes.md
context.text: Audit current uncommitted changes for concrete correctness problems. Do not modify files. Prioritize by impact and verify assumptions. Report only actionable issues introduced by the changes. Avoid speculative refactors and generic best practices. No findings means an empty findings array.

outputs.text:
Review the current uncommitted changes without modifying files. Report only verified, actionable correctness issues introduced by these changes; avoid speculative refactors.

Return one JSON object with a `findings` array, ordered by impact. Each finding contains `severity`, `file`, `line`, `issue`, and `recommendation`. If there are no findings, return `{"findings":[]}`. Do not add Markdown fences or other text.

Review the uncommitted changes for correctness. Keep the review **read-only** and verify assumptions before reporting an issue.

Return prioritized findings as JSON. Each finding should identify the problem, location, severity, and suggested correction. Do not include speculative refactors or general advice.

tasks.title: Unavailable-output state
tasks.request: Write a concise prompt asking an assistant to summarize an incident report without inventing a cause.

outputs.text: Summarize the supplied incident report. Separate confirmed facts from hypotheses, preserve the timeline, and identify unresolved questions. Do not invent a root cause. Return a concise summary with the incident’s impact and current status.
